<Rep. Rosa L. DeLauro, Rep. Grace Meng>: Pursuant to the provisions of clause 3(a)(1) of House rule XIII and sec. 6(i) of the Committee Rules, the dissenting views of the minority party of the House of Representatives, are printed below:
We appreciate Chairman Rogers's efforts this year as chair of the Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies (CJS) Subcommittee, including the hard work that has gone into the crafting of this appropriations bill. However, the harsh reality is that this bill does not fulfill the very real needs of the American people across a wide range of critical areas, including crime prevention; job creation; efforts to ensure fair trade; the advancement of American innovation and climate science research; and much more. Therefore, we must strongly oppose this bill in its current form.
This bill defunds law enforcement by gutting the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF) by more than 25 percent, forcing the agency to lose more than 1,000 law enforcement personnel nationwide. The bill also includes numerous harmful policy riders designed to further impede the efforts of law enforcement officers to fight gun violence, including a rider that completely shuts down the enforcement of all ATF measures, regulations, or guidance issued or finalized between January 2021 and January 2025. This will inevitably result in more illegal firearms trafficking, more guns falling into the hands of dangerous criminals, and more victims of gun violence in both large and small communities across our country.
Handicapping the ATF will also further burden our State and local law enforcement officers, who rely on their ATF counterparts to help them keep communities safe from gun violence.
In this bill, grants for local communities to prevent and respond to juvenile delinquency are also cut by $50 million below the current level. The bill further eliminates funding for Community Violence Intervention and Prevention grants and several other grants aimed at keeping communities safe.
Working Americans are facing a cost-of-living crisis that is only worsening. Yet the Majority's bill slashes funding for Economic Development Administration grants by 36 percent below the current level. These grants help create jobs and economic opportunity, improve public infrastructure, and ultimately help revitalize communities facing decline and disinvestment throughout our nation, particularly in rural areas. The bill also guts funding for the International Trade Administration. This will negatively impact the American economy in two ways:
(1) by reducing the agency's capacity to promote the expansion of U.S. exports, and (2) by degrading the agency's efforts to fight the unfair trade practices of other countries.
Perhaps most shortsighted of all, this bill makes deep cuts to the scientific research that drives American innovation, technological leadership, and economic competitiveness. At a time when other countries are increasing scientific investment to compete in the global economy, this bill cuts the National Science Foundation by more than $1.7 billion, sharply reducing cutting-edge American research and abandoning the next generation of scientists and engineers. NASA's Science account is cut by more than $1.3 billion, including a massive cut of $828 million (38 percent) to Earth Science, and NASA's Aeronautics research account is cut by $85 million, or 9 percent. The bill also makes massive cuts to the programs of the National Institute of Standards and Technology, which has helped American industry overcome technical challenges, innovate manufacturing, and work on the cutting edge of emerging technologies.
This bill also irresponsibly ignores the reality of global warming and the need for the United States to lead efforts to advance humanity's scientific understanding of climate change and our ability to prepare for, respond to, and mitigate its impacts. Such research also helps improve future weather forecasting, as carefully studying and tracking changes in the climate helps scientists better understand and predict the range of possible weather extremes, including the influence of the changing climate on extreme weather events such as hurricanes, wildfires, and flooding. In addition to the bill's huge cut to NASA Earth Science, the bill cuts funding for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)'s Climate Laboratories and Cooperative Institutes by 11 percent and cuts NOAA's Competitive Climate Research program by 23 percent.
As noted in a September 2023 report by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, ``climate change already imposes substantial financial costs on communities across the United States.'' According to NOAA, in 2024, the United States experienced 27 weather and climate disasters costing at least $1 billion each, totaling $182.7 billion. (The current Administration has unacceptably directed NOAA to discontinue compiling this statistic). In every decade since the 1980s, the average annual cost of these disasters has increased. Increasingly frequent extreme weather events disrupt crop yields, displace people from their homes, burden emergency service systems, and destroy critical infrastructure. However, the funding cuts in this bill turn a blind eye to this reality and will damage our capacity to improve the scientific understanding of our planet and its changes. This, in turn, will weaken our ability to protect the health and safety of Americans from climate change.
Within the NOAA program table, we also note with disappointment that the Majority is once again proposing to remove the name of former Representative Jose Serrano from NOAA's Educational Partnership Program with Minority Serving Institutions--in addition to sharply cutting this program's funding. Representative Serrano served for more than 30 years in Congress and was a distinguished former chair of the CJS Subcommittee.
The bill undermines efforts to promote justice and opportunity for all Americans. Besides gutting the Legal Services Corporation, which provides basic civil legal aid to the poorest American families, seniors, and veterans, the bill also drastically cuts funding for the Minority Business Development Agency and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. The Community Relations Service, which for more than 60 years has worked honorably to help mediate and end community conflicts across our country, is eliminated in this bill. Despite historically high levels of hate crimes recorded by the FBI, this bill eliminates DOJ programs aimed at preventing and prosecuting hate crimes. Furthermore, the bill prohibits funding for agency programs focused on diversity, equity, and inclusion.
The bill's funding level for the Census Bureau is very inadequate, especially as the Bureau must ramp up efforts in fiscal year 2027 to prepare for the 2027 Economic Census, the 2030 Decennial Census, and other census surveys. The bill also includes policy riders that would lower the quality of census surveys and implement an unconstitutional change to Census Bureau apportionment count procedures.
Furthermore, the bill continues the Majority's attacks on women's health and safety by barring funding for: (1) DOJ's Reproductive Rights Task Force, (2) enforcement of certain protections for women in the workplace, and (3) litigation against States or local governments over laws that limit access to abortion.
There are many additional harmful and irresponsible policy riders contained in this bill that must be removed, including riders impacting fisheries restoration, federal employee unions, and much more.
Last, but not least, we note that the lawless behavior of the current Administration requires that efforts be undertaken to ensure transparency and accountability. With that in mind, we are deeply distressed that this bill discontinues the requirement enacted in the Appropriations Acts for fiscal years 2025 and 2026 that agency spend plans must contain the same level of detail as provided in the spend plans for fiscal year 2024. We believe that the Appropriations Committee has a serious and vital duty to ensure transparency in the spending of taxpayer dollars, and removal of this provision is a dereliction of duty.
These and other issues must be addressed before this bill is enacted into law, and we stand ready to help improve the CJS appropriations bill for fiscal year 2027 in conference.
Rosa DeLauro.
Grace Meng.
